To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CytR protein prevents CRP protein to bind to its binding site in the udpP+ promoter, while in the udpP18 mutant the CRP protein binding site and CytR protein binding site overlap, and in the udpP1 mutant the CytR protein site is unaltered, while the CRP protein site is not.
the udp gene expression in E. coli is regulated by two independent regulatory systems, negative and positive.

(1) CytR protein is a repressor of udp gene expression in E. coli, and (2) CytR represses udp gene expression by interfering with the CRP-binding site in the promoter/operator region of the gene, thereby preventing the positive effect of cAMP-CPR complex on the udp gene expression
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the CytR and cAMP-CRP regulatory systems and provides evidence for the model proposed for the negative regulation of the udp gene expression
the interaction of CytR and CRP proteins in the regulation of the udp gene expression in Escherichiacoli.
the interaction of CytR and CRP proteins in the control of the expression of the uridine-phosphorylase gene of E. coli K-12.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crp(a), ptsG and cytR mutations are all capable of causing derepression of the udp gene in the presence of glucose, but only when the other two mutations are present simultaneously.
the udp gene is controlled by a negative regulatory system, which is dependent on the presence of the CytR protein.
CytR represses the udp gene expression in a manner that is dependent on the presence of cAMP-Crp complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the negative action of CytR represser protein is predominant over positive action of c AMP-CRP complex in the expression of the udp gene in the presence of glucose, while under the conditions of glucose limitation the positive action of the cAMP-CRP becomes dominant.

the crp(a)-mediated increase in the udpP+- and udpP1-lace expression is not due to the direct action of CRP protein on the corresponding promoter regions, but is rather a consequence of the increased expression of ptsG gene, which in turn leads to the decreased intracellular level of cAMP and thereby to a decreased repression of the udpP+-lac and udpP1 lac fusions by the cAMP-CRP protein complex.
the crp(a)-cytR- double mutant is constitutive in the expression of the udp gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CytR protein has a higher affinity to the promoter-operator region than CRP protein, and that the crp mutation alters the structure of the latter in such a way as to increase its affinity to this region.
the crp(a)-cytR double mutation results in constitutive expression of all three types of udp-lac fusions.
the crp(a)-cytR+ strain exhibits the same level of udp gene expression as the crp+cytR- strain.
